Question 2: Create two new categorical variables in flights based on the departure time (dep_time), and arrival time (arr_time). These new variables should have four categories: “early morning” for 12am to 6am, “morning” for 6am to 12pm, “afternoon” for 12pm to 6pm, and “evening” for 6pm to 12am. Show barplots of both of these new variables. What percentage of flights were “red eye” flights? We’ll define these as flights that depart in “afternoon” or “evening” and arrive in “early morning” or “morning.”

#extract the arrival and departure times, converting them into the proper numerical form
flights<-flights %>%
  filter(!is.na(dep_time),!is.na(arr_time))%>%
  mutate(
    hour_of_departure=dep_time%/%100,   
    hour_of_arrival=arr_time%/%100,   
#create periods/buckets for departing flights based on time windows given, use case_when() to evaluate the conditions in the hour of departure and arrival times and assign them as TRUE or FALSE based on the parameters. 
    departure_periods =case_when(
      hour_of_departure >= 0&hour_of_departure < 6~"Early Morning",
      hour_of_departure >= 6&hour_of_departure < 12~"Morning",
      hour_of_departure >= 12&hour_of_departure < 18~"Afternoon",
      hour_of_departure >= 18&hour_of_departure <= 23~"Evening",
      ),
#create periods/buckets for arriving flights based on time windows given
    arrival_periods = case_when(
      hour_of_arrival >= 0&hour_of_arrival < 6~"Early Morning",
      hour_of_arrival >= 6&hour_of_arrival < 12~"Morning",
      hour_of_arrival >= 12&hour_of_arrival < 18~"Afternoon",
      hour_of_arrival >= 18&hour_of_arrival <= 23~"Evening",
      ),overnight=arr_time<dep_time 
  )
  
#create barplots to show the newly created "departure_periods" and "arrival_periods" variables
BPD<-table(na.omit(flights$departure_periods))
#create barplot,titles,labels,and y-axis counts on bars
#barplot for departure categories
barplot_departures<-barplot(
  BPD,
  main="Departing Flights by Time Period",
  xlab="Period of Departure",
  ylab="Total Quantity of Flights",
  col=c("red","orange","yellow","green"),
  ylim=c(0,max(BPD)*1.3)
)
text(x=barplot_departures,y=BPD,label=format(BPD,big.mark=","),pos=3,cex=1
)
#barplot for arrival categories
BPA<-table(na.omit(flights$arrival_periods))
barplot_arrivals<-barplot(
  BPA,
  main="Arriving Flights by Time Period",
  xlab="Period of Arrival",
  ylab="Total Quantity of Flights",
  col=c("red","orange","yellow","green"),
  ylim=c(0,max(BPA)*1.3)
)
text(x=barplot_arrivals,y=BPA,label=format(BPD,big.mark=","),pos=3,cex=1
)
#total number of red eyes
red_eyes <- flights %>%
  filter(
    departure_periods %in% c("Afternoon", "Evening") &
    (arrival_periods %in% c("Early Morning", "Morning") | overnight)
  )
#calculate percent
red_eye_percent<-(nrow(red_eyes)/nrow(flights))*100
#display percent value
cat("Percentage of Flights that were Red-Eye:",red_eye_percent,"%\n")
Percentage of Flights that were Red-Eye: 3.232306 %

The tables generated display the total amount of Departing and Arriving flights in the respective categories: “Afternoon”, “Early Morning”, “Evening”, and “Morning”. The percentage of flights that were red-eye is 3.23%.

Question 3: Where there any planes that flew for multiple airlines? If so, how many were there and which airlines did they fly for?

#create object, filter by tail number, remove flights with missing tail no.
planes_multiple_carriers<-flights%>%
  filter(!is.na(tailnum))%>%       
  group_by(tailnum)%>%
  #count the number of planes and the distinct carriers/airlines they flew for
  summarize(
    num_airlines=n_distinct(carrier),  
    airlines=paste(sort(unique(carrier)),collapse=", ")
    )%>%
  filter(num_airlines > 1) %>%       
  arrange(desc(num_airlines))

Question 4: In the figure above, there is a missing relationship between weather and airports. What is the relationship and how should it appear in the diagram?

The relationship adds new layers to the current diagram. ‘weather’ contains weather data respective to each airport being observed. There are many weather observations respective to each airport being examined. This means that an arrow should be drawn and added to the diagram that connects ‘weather’ to ‘airports’.

Question 5: In order to address our primary question, we want to prepare a tidy dataset (a single data frame). This will consist of information from the flights and weather data. The year, month, day, hour, and origin variables from weather provide almost enough information to give each observation a unique value. Create a new variable in the weather dataset by pasting together those 5 variables, then determine how many duplicated values there are and explain why.

tidy_weather<-weather %>%
  mutate(weatherID=paste(year,month,day,hour,origin,sep = "_"))

duplicated_values<-sum(duplicated(tidy_weather$weatherID))
cat("Number of Duplicated Values:",duplicated_values,"\n")
Number of Duplicated Values: 3 
duplicates_list<-tidy_weather %>%
  count(weatherID)%>%
  filter(n > 1)%>%
  arrange(desc(n))  

cat("Number of unique duplicated weatherID combinations:", nrow(duplicates_list),"\n\n")
Number of unique duplicated weatherID combinations: 3 
print(duplicates_list)

#correlation analysis between the different weather factors in relation to arrivals and departures
correlations<-weather_factors%>%
  summarize(across(temp:visib,~cor(.,dep_delay,use= "complete.obs"),.names="departure_correlations_{col}"))%>%
  bind_cols(weather_factors%>%
      summarize(across(temp:visib,~cor(.,arr_delay,use="complete.obs"),.names="arrival_correlations_{col}"))
  )%>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable",values_to="correlation")%>%
  mutate(type=ifelse(str_detect(variable,"departure_"),"Departure Delay","Arrival Delay"),
         variable = str_remove(variable, "departure_correlations_|arrival_correlations_"))
print(correlations)

Question 7: Calculate the average departure delay for each day (Hint: think about which variables you need in order to do this!). Which day had the worst average length of delay for departures? Now calculate the averages by day and origin. Which airport had the worst single day for delays and when was it? Now calculate the averages by hour and origin. Which airport had the worst single hour for delays (and when was it)?

#Calculate the average departure delay for each day
avg_daily_delay<-flights_new %>%
  group_by(year.x,month.x,day.x) %>%
  summarize(avg_departure_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),.groups="drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_departure_delay))
#Which day had the worst average length of delay for departures?
worst_day<-avg_daily_delay%>%
  slice_max(avg_departure_delay,n=1)
print(worst_day)

  arrange(desc(avg_departure_delay))

Question 8: Compute the average delay by destination, then add that information to the airports data frame. Make a map showing the spatial distribution of delays (you can make it however you like, but we recommend using either ggplot or leaflet). Use the color of the points to display the average delay for each airport.

#Compute the average delay by destination
average_delay_destination<-flights_new%>%
  group_by(dest)%>%
  summarize(average_arrival_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),.groups="drop")
#Add the information to the airports data frame
average_delay_destination<-airports %>%
  left_join(average_delay_destination,by=c("faa"="dest"))

leaflet(average_delay_destination) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = ~ lon, lat = ~lat,color=~ifelse(average_arrival_delay>0,"red","blue"),radius=~pmin(abs(average_arrival_delay)/5,10),popup=~paste0("<b>",name,"</b><br>Avg Delay: ",round(average_arrival_delay,1)," min"))%>%
  addLegend("bottomright", colors = c("blue", "red"),labels=c("On-Time/Early Arrival","Delayed Arrival"),title="Average Arrival Delays by Airport")

Question 9: Finally, create as many plots and summary statistics as needed to answer the primary question above

#create categories/buckets for temperatures seen in the columns that highlight temp, pressure, humidity, wind sp., visibility, and precipitation, regard for infinite and negative infinite values.
weather_delay_stat_summary<-flights_new%>%
  mutate(
    temp_category=cut(temp,breaks=c(-Inf,32,60,80,Inf),labels=c("Extremely Cold","Cool","Warm","Extremely Hot")),
    pressure_category=cut(pressure,breaks=c(-Inf,1000,1015,1030,Inf),labels=c("Low","Normal","High","Extremely High")),
    humidity_category=cut(humid,breaks=c(-Inf,40,70,Inf),labels =c("Low","Normal","High")),
    wind_speed_category=cut(wind_speed,breaks=c(-Inf,5,15,25,Inf),labels=c("Low","Calm","Blustery","Extremely Windy")),
    visibility_category=cut(visib, breaks=c(-Inf,2,5,10,Inf),labels=c("Low","Moderate","Good","Excellent")),
    precip_category=cut(precip,breaks=c(-Inf,0,0.1,0.5,Inf),labels=c("None","Light","Moderate","Heavy"))
  )
#find the average departure and arrival delay period for each weather factor
stat_summary_weather_category<-list(
  Temperature = weather_delay_stat_summary%>%
    group_by(temp_category)%>%
    summarize(avg_dep_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),avg_arr_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),n=n()),
   Pressure=weather_delay_stat_summary%>%
    group_by(pressure_category)%>%
    summarize(avg_dep_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),avg_arr_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),n=n()),
  Humidity=weather_delay_stat_summary%>%
    group_by(humidity_category)%>%
    summarize(avg_dep_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),avg_arr_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),n=n()),
  Wind_Speed=weather_delay_stat_summary%>%
    group_by(wind_speed_category)%>%
    summarize(avg_dep_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),avg_arr_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),n=n()),
  Visibility=weather_delay_stat_summary%>%
    group_by(visibility_category)%>%
    summarize(avg_dep_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),avg_arr_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),n=n()),
  Precipitation=weather_delay_stat_summary%>%
    group_by(precip_category)%>%
    summarize(avg_dep_delay=mean(dep_delay,na.rm=TRUE),avg_arr_delay=mean(arr_delay,na.rm=TRUE),n=n())
)
